notes.text: A flaw was found in pyasn1, a generic ASN.1 library for Python. The Basic Encoding Rules (BER) decoder, used by CER and DER codecs, processes long-form tags by accumulating continuation octets without an upper bound. A remote attacker can exploit this by providing a specially crafted input, leading to the construction of an arbitrarily large integer. This can cause the CPU cost to grow quadratically, resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS) for any application decoding untrusted BER, CER, or DER input.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: python-pyasn1: pyasn1: Denial of Service via crafted BER input
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw was found in pyasn1's BER decoder. The decoder parses long-form tags by accumulating continuation octets without an upper bound, allowing crafted input to force construction of an arbitrarily large integer with quadratic CPU cost. On Python 3.11+, this can also trigger unhandled ValueError exceptions. Exploitation requires that an application passes untrusted BER, CER, or DER input directly to the pyasn1 decoder — pyasn1 is a library and does not independently accept network input. Many common uses of pyasn1 involve parsing trusted certificates or local configuration and are not exposed to this flaw. The realistic impact is a denial-of-service of the consuming Python process, with automatic recovery in typical service deployments.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Netty (io.netty:netty-handler). When using the SslProvider.OPENSSL client path with a plain X509TrustManager and without Unsafe-based trust-manager wrapping (Java 25+), TLS hostname verification is disabled. This misconfiguration allows a man-in-the-middle attacker to present a fraudulent certificate for a different hostname, which is then accepted without proper validation. This could lead to sensitive information disclosure.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: io.netty/netty-handler: Netty: TLS hostname verification bypass via OpenSSL client path misconfiguration
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat products ship io.netty:netty-handler as a transitive dependency across multiple middleware and platform products. While the CVSS score reflects the severity of a successful exploit — full confidentiality compromise of TLS-protected traffic without authentication — the vulnerable code path requires three conditions simultaneously: explicit OpenSSL provider configuration, a plain X509TrustManager, and a Java 25+ runtime. Most Red Hat product deployments use the default JDK SSL provider and currently run on Java 21 LTS, making the vulnerable configuration uncommon in practice.

This vulnerability only affects applications that explicitly configure Netty to use the OpenSSL TLS provider (SslProvider.OPENSSL). 

The following mitigations can reduce exposure without applying a patch:

1) Use the default JDK SSL provider — Do not configure SslProvider.OPENSSL in your Netty SslContext setup. The default JDK SSL provider (SslProvider.JDK) is not affected by this vulnerability. Most applications use the JDK default unless explicitly overridden.

2) Use X509ExtendedTrustManager — If the OpenSSL provider is required, ensure the configured trust manager extends X509ExtendedTrustManager rather than the plain X509TrustManager interface. The extended variant performs hostname verification independently of the Netty wrapping logic.

3) Run on Java 24 or earlier — The vulnerable code path only triggers on Java 25+ where sun.misc.Unsafe-based trust-manager wrapping is unavailable. Running on earlier Java versions (e.g., Java 21 LTS) means the wrapping works correctly and hostname verification stays enabled.

By submitting crafted form data with excessively nested bracket-delimited field names, an attacker can trigger uncontrolled recursion in the formDataToJSON function (exposed as axios.formToJSON() and used internally by the default transformRequest when FormData is sent with Content-Type: application/json), exhausting the JavaScript call stack and causing a RangeError that may terminate the application process. This vulnerability affects applications that pass attacker-controlled FormData field names to axios' FormData-to-JSON conversion.

notes.text: A flaw was found in fast-uri, a URI parser for Node.js. Its custom parser for bracketed IPv6 literals does not fully validate the IPv6 grammar, allowing invalid trailing text in an authority to be silently discarded. This can lead to a malformed, attacker-controlled host being normalized into a different, valid IPv6 destination, such as a local or private IPv6 target. This could allow an attacker to bypass URL allowlists or network-based access controls, potentially enabling unauthorized access to internal services, cloud metadata endpoints, or other network resources. This issue affects Red Hat products that bundle fast-uri as part of their Node.js dependencies. Fixed versions are available: fast-uri 2.4.5, 3.1.6, and 4.1.3.

notes.text: A flaw was found in fast-uri, a software component used for parsing Uniform Resource Identifiers (URIs) in Node.js applications. This vulnerability arises from an issue in how fast-uri processes the scheme part of a URI, specifically when it contains special characters that are percent-encoded. An attacker can exploit this by crafting a malicious URI, causing the parser to misinterpret the host, which can lead to serious security risks. These risks include unauthorized redirection to external websites, server-side request forgery (SSRF) where the application makes unintended requests to internal or external resources, and bypassing security policies.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: fast-uri: fast-uri: URI parsing flaw enables server-side request forgery and redirects
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A host confusion vulnerability was found in fast-uri, a URI parser for Node.js. The parser runs a legacy decoding pass over the scheme component and never re-escapes the result. As a consequence, an input whose scheme carries percent-encoded slashes parses as having no authority (undefined host), yet resolving or normalizing that same input emits a network-path reference with an attacker-chosen authority. Applications that normalize or resolve untrusted URLs before a redirect check, host allowlist, or outbound request decision can be steered to an attacker-controlled domain, enabling server-side request forgery (SSRF), open redirect, or address-policy bypass. Additionally, a normalized URI in a response header can carry injected carriage return line feed (CRLF) characters, enabling HTTP response splitting attacks such as cache poisoning or session hijacking. This issue affects Red Hat products that bundle fast-uri as part of their Node.js dependencies. Fixed versions are available: fast-uri 2.4.5, 3.1.6, and 4.1.3.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: GitPython before 3.1.59 fails to safely re-serialize multi-line git-config values during write operations, corrupting dormant quoted values into injected directives like core.hooksPath. notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: gitpython: GitPython before 3.1.59 Remote Code Execution via Config Injection
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
Case for AC:H (8.1): the trigger needs two things the attacker does not
  straightforwardly own:
    (1) a crafted multi-line quoted value must already sit DORMANT in .git/config
        — the guarded set_value() path will not put it there; it must arrive via
        _read() of a file the attacker influenced but does not directly write; and
    (2) a SUBSEQUENT, UNRELATED GitPython config WRITE must fire to re-serialize
        and corrupt it — and that write is performed by the victim application on
        its own schedule, not by the attacker. 
    "Prepare the target environment" + "conditions beyond the attacker's control"
    is the textbook AC:H definition; step (2) in particular fits it.

notes.text: A flaw was found in GitPython. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to create arbitrary Git directories outside the intended clone destination. By manipulating the `separate_git_dir` parameter during repository cloning, an attacker can redirect repository metadata to an attacker-controlled filesystem path. This could lead to arbitrary directory creation and potentially enable the execution of malicious code through Git hooks.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: GitPython: GitPython: Arbitrary Code Execution via Path Traversal
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat Product Security has identified a path traversal vulnerability in GitPython versions before 3.1.59. The vulnerability arises because the `--separate-git-dir` option is not included in the `unsafe_git_clone_options` denylist, allowing attackers who control the `separate_git_dir` parameter during repository cloning to redirect Git repository metadata to arbitrary filesystem locations outside the intended clone destination. This can lead to arbitrary directory and file creation bounded only by process permissions. When combined with subsequent Git operations that trigger hook execution on the redirected repository, this vulnerability can escalate to arbitrary code execution. Exploitation requires that the application passes untrusted, attacker-controlled input to the `separate_git_dir` keyword argument of `Repo.clone_from()` or `Repo.clone()` methods without proper validation, while the `allow_unsafe_options` parameter remains at its default value of False.

The vulnerability occurs because the urllib.parse.parse_qs function is used without limiting the maximum number of fields.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw was found in Tornado's request body parsing mechanism. Parsing these fields synchronously blocks Tornado's single-threaded event loop, leading to a complete denial of service for all concurrent connections and incoming requests.

notes.text: A denial of service vulnerability was found in the qs package for Node.js. The stringify function does not verify that constructor.isBuffer is callable before invoking it. An attacker who can influence object shape, for example through query parameters parsed with allowPrototypes: true as Express 4 does by default, can cause qs.stringify to throw a TypeError when that data is re-serialized. In typical Node.js HTTP frameworks the error is caught per request and returns HTTP 500. In code paths without an error boundary, such as async handlers or background jobs, the process may exit.

Servers created with xds.NewGRPCServer() can be exploited by a remote client sending a malformed RPC request that lacks the required :authority or Host headers. This can trigger an index-out-of-bounds panic, leading to the termination of the entire server process and a Denial of Service (DoS). In some deployments, this attack can be unauthenticated.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: google.golang.org/grpc: gRPC-Go: Denial of Service via malformed RPC requests
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity impact because an unauthenticated remote client can crash the host daemon, causing an immediate denial of service across exposed endpoints. The issue specifically threatens deployments utilizing xDS-managed gRPC servers, as requests that omit standard routing authority parameters cause the application to crash on an unhandled slice lookup. Standard gRPC server implementations that do not configure xDS control plane routing are not susceptible to this failure mode. Furthermore, in environments enforcing mutual transport layer security (mTLS), successful transport authentication is required before reaching the vulnerable routing stage, restricting potential exploitation to authenticated peers.

notes.text: A flaw was found in undici's BalancedPool component. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to bypass Transport Layer Security (TLS) certificate validation. The BalancedPool constructor incorrectly processes its options, silently discarding custom certificate validation functions. Consequently, a peer with an otherwise untrusted certificate may be accepted, potentially compromising the integrity of secure communication.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: undici: undici: TLS certificate validation bypass in BalancedPool via dropped connect options
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This flaw only affects applications that construct an undici BalancedPool with a function-valued connect or tls option — for example, a custom checkServerIdentity callback or connector used for certificate pinning across multiple upstreams. Client, Pool, Agent, and RoundRobinPool destructure these options before the internal JSON-based clone and are not affected. An attacker able to present, on the network path, a TLS endpoint whose certificate the application's custom validator was written to reject — but which still satisfies Node.js's default hostname and chain checks — can have that certificate silently accepted when the connection goes through BalancedPool, enabling a man-in-the-middle attack against affected connections.
This affects undici versions from 7.24.1 up to 7.29.1 and from 8.0.0 up to 8.10.2.
notes.title: Statement

cwe.name: Origin Validation Error

notes.text: A flaw was found in undici. When the cache or deduplicate interceptor is directly composed onto a Client or Pool, the destination origin is omitted from cache and request-deduplication keys. This allows a remote attacker to perform cross-origin cache poisoning, leading to information disclosure and potentially a full authentication bypass. An attacker could exploit this by having a trusted origin accept a malicious token, without contacting the legitimate trusted origin.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: undici: undici: Authentication bypass via cross-origin cache poisoning due to missing origin isolation
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This flaw is present in the undici HTTP client library used by Node.js. When an application composes undici's Cache or Deduplicate interceptor directly onto a Client or Pool object (rather than onto an Agent), the library's internal cache and in-flight-request deduplication keys omit the destination origin. As a result, a cached or in-flight response captured for one upstream origin can be returned for a request intended for a different, trusted origin whenever the method, path, and relevant headers match. In the most severe demonstrated scenario, this allowed an attacker-controlled JWT to be accepted by the application as though it had been validated against a legitimate, trusted issuer, without that issuer ever being contacted — resulting in a full authentication bypass.
Exploitation requires that the affected application attach the Cache or Deduplicate interceptor directly to a Client/Pool — the default Agent-based dispatch path is not affected, since Agent already carries the origin in its dispatch options — and that an attacker can influence or collide with the cache/deduplication key for at least one origin the application communicates with.).
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in odh-dashboard in Red Hat OpenShift AI. The backend-for-frontend route GET /api/nim-serving/:nimResource reads Kubernetes Secrets using the dashboard service account and returns the full Secret object, including .data, without an authorization check. Any authenticated dashboard user can retrieve the cluster NVIDIA NGC API key Secret (apiKeySecret) and the NIM image pull secret (nimPullSecret). Create and delete of the same NIM credential are admin-gated; the read path is not. This is missing authorization (CWE-862) and insufficiently protected credentials (CWE-522). It is distinct from CVE-2026-5483 (service-account token leak in the Kubernetes client response wrapper on the same route) and CVE-2026-16456 (odh-model-controller cross-namespace confused deputy).
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: odh-dashboard: odh-dashboard: NIM credential Secret readable by any authenticated user
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This Moderate vulnerability in odh-dashboard allows an authenticated, non-admin OpenShift AI dashboard user to read cluster-global NVIDIA NGC / NIM credentials. The GET /api/nim-serving/:nimResource handler uses the dashboard service account to fetch Secrets and returns Secret .data. Sibling NIM create/delete routes use secureAdminRoute; this read path does not. Exploitation requires a logged-in dashboard session and a configured NIM Account. The leaked credentials are shared infrastructure secrets, not per-user. CVE-2026-5483 addressed a different leak (dashboard SA token in the full k8s client response) on the same endpoint and did not add an authorization guard or strip Secret .data.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the GridFS component of the MongoDB Python Driver (pymongo). The driver can treat a caller-supplied structured file identifier as a MongoDB query condition instead of a literal identifier. An authenticated user who can influence the identifier passed to GridFS download, delete, or rename operations may retrieve stored file content beyond the intended target, delete all GridFS chunks in the affected bucket (rendering stored files unreadable), or rename a file other than the intended target.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: pymongo: MongoDB Python Driver: Data disclosure and denial of service via query-operator injection
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This vulnerability is rated as Important because an authenticated user who can influence a GridFS file identifier can delete all file chunks in the affected bucket, making stored files unreadable, and can retrieve or rename a file other than the intended target. Exploitation requires an application to pass a structured identifier, for example a dictionary containing MongoDB query operators, into GridFS download, delete, or rename APIs rather than a literal identifier such as an ObjectId or string.

pymongo is a client library. A deployment is exploitable only if it calls those GridFS APIs with attacker-influenced identifiers. Scalar identifiers are not interpreted as query conditions. Successful exploitation is limited to GridFS-stored file content. It does not by itself provide code execution or host compromise.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in google-protobuf. An unauthenticated remote attacker can send a specially crafted message containing deeply nested protobuf group fields to a Node.js service using the affected library. This uncontrolled recursion can cause the service to crash, leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) for legitimate users.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: google-protobuf: google-protobuf: Denial of Service via uncontrolled recursion in protobuf group field parsing
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw was found in the google-protobuf (protobuf-javascript) npm package, which Red Hat OpenShift AI (RHOAI) ships bundled in its container images. When parsing unknown protobuf group fields, the BinaryReader.skipGroup() and skipField() functions call each other recursively without any recursion depth limit. An unauthenticated remote attacker can send a small, specially crafted message containing deeply nested START_GROUP wire bytes to a Node.js service that passes attacker-controlled data to the generated deserializeBinary() API, causing a RangeError (maximum call stack size exceeded) that crashes the Node.js process and results in a denial of service. No authentication or prior knowledge of the protobuf schema is required. Only availability is affected; there is no impact on confidentiality or integrity. Red Hat rates this issue as IMPORTANT severity (CVSS 3.1 score 7.5); the upstream advisory scores it 8.7 using CVSS 4.0, and the difference is attributable to the CVSS version used rather than a materially different view of the vulnerability. Within Red Hat, google-protobuf is consumed through RHOAI container images rather than shipped as a standalone product; the affected RHOAI components are handled with delegated resolution and the responsible product team is pursuing a fix.

notes.text: A flaw was found in FasterXML jackson-databind. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by providing specially crafted JSON input to an application that deserializes it into an identity-enabled collection or map. The flaw occurs due to inefficient processing of forward-references, where the system performs a quadratic amount of work for linearly growing input, leading to excessive CPU consumption.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: com.fasterxml.jackson.core/jackson-databind: tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind: Jackson-databind: Denial of Service via quadratic forward-reference completion
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in jackson-databind. Forward-reference completion for `@JsonIdentityInfo` object IDs in `CollectionDeserializer.CollectionReferringAccumulator.resolveForwardReference()` and the equivalent implementation in `MapDeserializer` performs a linear scan of the pending-reference accumulator for every resolved ID.

When a document creates unresolved object-ID references in an identity-enabled collection or map and then defines those IDs in reverse order, completion performs quadratic CPU work, allowing an attacker to cause a Denial of Service by sending specially crafted JSON input.

Exploitation requires an application that deserializes attacker-influenced JSON into an `@JsonIdentityInfo`-annotated collection or map.

The fix replaces the repeated linear lookup with a keyed pending-reference structure.

notes.text: A flaw was found in JupyterLab. This vulnerability allows Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) when pasting notebook cells from the system clipboard, as the application fails to clear trusted metadata flags from imported cell data. A remote attacker could exploit this by enticing a user to paste malicious cell content, bypassing output sanitization. Successful exploitation enables the execution of arbitrary scripts within the user's authenticated session, potentially leading to unauthorized actions and information disclosure.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: jupyterlab: JupyterLab: Cross-Site Scripting via malicious clipboard cell pasting
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An IMPORTANT severity cross-site scripting (XSS) flaw was found in JupyterLab, which Red Hat ships within Red Hat OpenShift AI (RHOAI) and Migration Toolkit for Applications offerings. When the useSystemClipboardForCells setting is enabled and pasteCodeCellsWithoutOutput is disabled (the default), the system clipboard cell-paste path accepts attacker-controlled cell JSON without clearing metadata.trusted. A pasted code cell can therefore mark its HTML output as trusted, bypass output sanitization, and execute attacker-supplied script in the authenticated JupyterLab origin as soon as the cell is pasted, without the user executing it. Running in the victim's session, the script can call the Jupyter Server REST API as that user, reading and writing any file under the server root, starting a kernel and running code in it, and opening a terminal where terminals are enabled. A remote attacker needs no JupyterLab account and no access to the server; exploitation requires enticing a user to copy malicious content and paste it into JupyterLab. Markdown and raw cells are not affected because their output is always sanitized. Red Hat's CVSS 3.1 score of 8.1 (IMPORTANT) matches the upstream score and reflects JupyterLab 4.5.0 and 4.5.1, where the system clipboard path is always active; from 4.5.2 the useSystemClipboardForCells setting is off by default, which lowers the practical attack complexity for deployments that keep that default. JupyterLab releases prior to 4.5.0, such as those bundled in some Red Hat OpenShift AI images, are not affected because the vulnerable system clipboard paste path was introduced in 4.5.0. This issue is delegated to the responsible Red Hat product teams and a fix is being pursued.

notes.text: A flaw was found in virtualenv. The generated activation scripts for shells such as bash, zsh, and fish apply improper quoting to environment and library path variables. An attacker can exploit this by providing a crafted virtual environment path containing shell metacharacters. When an unsuspecting user sources the activation script, the embedded metacharacters are executed as shell commands, leading to arbitrary code execution with the privileges of that user.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: virtualenv: virtualenv: Arbitrary code execution via crafted paths in activation scripts
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: An Important severity flaw was found in virtualenv, a tool for creating isolated Python virtual environments that is bundled as a dependency in a number of Red Hat products, including Red Hat OpenShift AI, Red Hat Enterprise Linux container images, Red Hat Hardened Images, and other Red Hat-delivered components. The generated activate (bash and zsh) and activate.fish scripts place path values that were already escaped by shlex.quote inside an additional quoted context. The surplus quotes can terminate the data-only quoted run, leaving shell metacharacters within a crafted value to be parsed as shell commands: in the bash and zsh scripts a crafted virtual environment path is interpolated when a relocated environment's recorded directory is absent, and in the fish script crafted Tcl or Tk library paths are interpolated into __TCL_LIBRARY__ or __TK_LIBRARY__. When a user sources such an activation script, an attacker who controls the crafted path can execute arbitrary code with the privileges of that user. The flaw was rated Important (CVSS 3.1 score 7.8, AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H), consistent with the upstream severity; exploitation requires local control of the affected path values and user interaction to source the activation script. notes.text: An Important severity flaw was found in virtualenv, a tool for creating isolated Python virtual environments that is shipped in Red Hat products and offerings including Red Hat Enterprise Linux, Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform, Red Hat AI offerings, and other Red Hat cloud services. When virtualenv fetches pip or setuptools seed wheels over the network, through its periodic-update mechanism or the --download option, it does not verify the downloaded files against an authoritative cryptographic checksum. notes.text: An IMPORTANT severity command injection flaw was found in virtualenv, a tool for creating isolated Python virtual environments that is shipped as a bundled dependency in Red Hat offerings such as Red Hat OpenShift AI, Red Hat Enterprise Linux UBI container images, Red Hat Hardened Images components, and Fedora/EPEL community projects. notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw was found in virtualenv, a tool for creating isolated Python virtual environments that is bundled in a number of Red Hat offerings, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux, Red Hat OpenShift AI, and other layered products and containers, as well as in Fedora and EPEL community builds. Red Hat rates this flaw as having Moderate impact. virtualenv writes prompt values verbatim into the line-oriented pyvenv.cfg file, while its reader parses the file with str.splitlines() and accepts the last value for duplicate keys. An attacker who can influence prompt input -- the --prompt command-line option, the VIRTUALENV_PROMPT environment variable, or a configuration-derived value such as a CI job templating an untrusted branch name -- can inject line boundaries and additional configuration keys, including home, into the generated pyvenv.cfg. Because tooling reads home to locate the base interpreter, a consumer that trusts the file can be redirected to an attacker-selected interpreter, potentially resulting in arbitrary code execution or environment tampering when the virtual environment is used. Exploitation requires the prompt value to come from outside the operator's trust boundary: where the operator supplies the prompt directly, they already control the command line, and the effect is corruption of their own environment rather than privilege gain. This is why Red Hat assesses the impact as Moderate, while the upstream project published the advisory with low severity. Fixes for affected Red Hat products and streams are being pursued by the responsible component and product teams under delegated resolution; some community and out-of-support-scope streams will not receive an update.

notes.text: tornado: Tornado: Denial of Service via decompression bomb in CurlAsyncHTTPClient
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability has been rated as Important because an untrusted remote server can remotely terminate an application process through memory exhaustion without requiring credentials. By default, Tornado deploys the SimpleAsyncHTTPClient implementation, which includes built-in thresholds for decompressed and raw payload sizes and remains unaffected by this flaw. However, systems that explicitly configure CurlAsyncHTTPClient—typically enabled for custom proxy routing or advanced transport options—bypass these protections and do not enforce body size constraints. When such client applications fetch resources from compromised or malicious web endpoints, the resulting decompression bomb can consume all available system memory, leading to an immediate denial of service.

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

remediations.details:
For Red Hat OpenShift AI 2.25.12 see the following documentation, which will be updated shortly for this release, for important instructions on how to upgrade your cluster and fully apply this errata update:

https://docs.redhat.com/en/documentation/red_hat_openshift_ai/

Restrict outbound HTTP client requests to trusted destinations and avoid using the CurlAsyncHTTPClient backend when fetching untrusted web content.

1. Application configuration: Configure Tornado applications to utilize the default SimpleAsyncHTTPClient instead of CurlAsyncHTTPClient, provided specialized libcurl functionality (such as custom proxy configurations or specific TLS options) is not required. The default client enforces strict size boundaries on compressed and uncompressed response bodies.
2. Network egress filtering: Implement firewall rules or egress network policies to restrict outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections exclusively to verified, trustworthy endpoints, preventing the client from contacting potentially malicious third-party servers.
3. Operational controls: Ensure that user-supplied or untrusted URLs are validated, sanitized, or rejected before initiating outbound retrieval requests.

Caveats: Switching the HTTP client backend from CurlAsyncHTTPClient to SimpleAsyncHTTPClient may disrupt services that depend on libcurl-specific features. Enforcing egress filtering may block connections to unlisted external services.

notes.text: A flaw was found in fsspec. This vulnerability can lead to arbitrary code execution due to unrestricted template evaluation in the ReferenceFileSystem component. When processing filesystem reference metadata documents, template expressions are evaluated without security restrictions or sandboxing. A remote attacker can exploit this flaw by enticing a user or automated service to open a maliciously crafted reference file, resulting in arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the running application.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: fsspec: fsspec: arbitrary code execution via unrestricted template rendering in ReferenceFileSystem
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important severity flaw because an attacker could achieve arbitrary code execution within the application environment, though exploitation requires tricking a user or pipeline into opening an untrusted reference catalog. In typical Red Hat deployments such as Red Hat OpenShift AI (RHOAI), fsspec is utilized for data manipulation and storage abstraction across containerized workloads. The impact is limited to the privileges of the running container or application process without granting immediate host-level access, which aligns the risk with an Important rather than a Critical rating.

notes.text: A flaw was found in docling. When configured to process LaTeX documents using the Tectonic engine, the application does not restrict TeX file operations during compilation. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by submitting crafted document input to read sensitive files or overwrite existing files on the host system. In environments where shell escape features are enabled, this flaw may also permit arbitrary command execution.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: docling: docling: Arbitrary file read and write via unrestricted TeX primitives in Tectonic engine
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A moderate severity vulnerability was found in docling, a document conversion library shipped in Red Hat OpenShift AI and Lightspeed Core offerings. When docling is explicitly configured to render LaTeX content with the Tectonic engine (LatexBackendOptions(tikz_engine="tectonic")), it compiles an untrusted TikZ body and document preamble without restricting TeX file primitives such as \openin and \openout. An attacker who can supply a crafted document for conversion can use these primitives to read files accessible to the converter process and to create or overwrite writable files on the host, impacting confidentiality, integrity, and availability. If the separate tikz_engine_allow_shell_escape option is also enabled, arbitrary command execution through TeX shell escapes is possible. The default docling configuration, which does not enable Tectonic rendering, is not affected. Red Hat rates this flaw moderate, lower than the upstream important rating, because exploitation requires a non-default configuration that explicitly enables the Tectonic engine and requires processing attacker-supplied input, resulting in a local attack vector with high attack complexity and required user interaction rather than the network vector assumed upstream. The affected Red Hat products are tracked as affected and fixes are being pursued through the responsible product teams.

Avoid enabling the Tectonic TikZ engine when processing untrusted LaTeX documents. The default docling configuration does not enable Tectonic rendering and is not affected by this flaw, so deployments that have not opted into LatexBackendOptions(tikz_engine="tectonic") are not exposed. The tikz_engine_allow_shell_escape option, which additionally allows shell command execution through TeX, should not be enabled. cwe.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

notes.text: A flaw was found in the net/http package of the Golang standard library. The HTTP client drops sensitive headers after following a cross-domain redirect. For example, a request to `a.com/` containing an Authorization header redirected to `b.com/` will not send that header to `b.com`. However, the sensitive headers would be restored if the client received a subsequent same-domain redirect. For example, a chain of redirects from `a.com/`, to `b.com/1`, and finally to `b.com/2` would incorrectly send the Authorization header to `b.com/2`.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: net/http: net/http: sensitive headers incorrectly sent after cross-domain redirect
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact: Red Hat products that include the affected golang net/http client are affected by a credential-disclosure flaw in HTTP redirect handling. When a client request with a sensitive header such as Authorization is redirected from one domain to another and then to a same-domain URL, the client can incorrectly restore and send that header to the final destination, potentially exposing credentials and other sensitive information. The current Red Hat scope contains affected entries across Red Hat Enterprise Linux, OpenShift Container Platform, and other Red Hat products and components; some affect records have a current NOTAFFECTED resolution, indicating those specific product/version records are not affected, but the record provides no technical justification for why. For affected entries marked DELEGATED, a fix is being pursued by the responsible product teams. For entries marked DEFER, the record does not establish a product-specific reason for deferral; the residual risk is that applications using the affected net/http client can still disclose sensitive headers through this redirect sequence. Red Hat's CVSS is 5.9 Moderate (AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N), compared with CISA's 6.1 Moderate, reflecting Red Hat's higher attack-complexity and unchanged-scope assessment and confidentiality-only impact.

notes.text: A flaw was found in net/http. Handling Proxy-Authorization and Proxy-Authenticate headers during cross-origin redirects allows these headers to be inadvertently forwarded, potentially exposing sensitive authentication credentials. This flaw allows a network-based attacker to manipulate redirect responses, unintentionally exposing authentication details to unauthorized parties.

Successful exploitation requires a specific set of circumstances, including the use of a proxy that relies on these headers for authentication and a user being enticed to interact with a malicious URL. The vulnerability does not allow for arbitrary code execution or a direct compromise of system integrity or availability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Golang crypto/internal/nistec package. Due to the usage of a variable time instruction in the assembly implementation of an internal function, a small number of bits of secret scalars are leaked on the ppc64le architecture. Considering how this function is used, this leakage is likely insufficient to recover the private key when P-256 is used in any well-known protocols.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/internal/nistec: golang: Timing sidechannel for P-256 on ppc64le in crypto/internal/nistec
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact: Red Hat product builds using the Golang crypto/internal/nistec component on ppc64le are exposed to a timing side channel. A variable-time instruction in an internal assembly function leaks a small number of bits of secret scalars; given how the function is used, the leakage is likely insufficient to recover a private key when P-256 is used in well-known protocols. The current affects cover Red Hat Enterprise Linux, OpenShift Container Platform, and other Red Hat products, while entries resolved as Not a Bug, Obsolete, or delegated NOTAFFECTED are outside the actionable affected scope. For the DEFER entries, remediation is deferred because the leakage is not believed sufficient for private-key recovery in those protocols; the residual risk is limited scalar-bit leakage on ppc64le. For DELEGATED entries, the same Moderate impact is being handled by the relevant product teams, with a fix being pursued. Red Hat's CVSS is 5.3 Moderate with a network attack vector, compared with CISA's 4.0 Moderate local-vector assessment.

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. This vulnerability allows improper certificate validation, bypassing policy constraints via using ExtKeyUsageAny in VerifyOptions.KeyUsages.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: Usage of ExtKeyUsageAny disables policy validation in crypto/x509
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This flaw is rated as an Important severity because the vulnerability was found in the certificate validation logic of the Verify function. When VerifyOptions.KeyUsages includes ExtKeyUsageAny, certificate chains containing policy graphs may bypass certificate policy validation. This flaw allows an attacker to trick the system into accepting an invalid certificate, potentially enabling spoofing attacks, the issue weakens trust decisions in affected cases and impacts system integrity. Confidentiality and availability are not affected.

Red Hat Openshift Container Platform openshift-golang-builder-container ships golang 1.23 and does not ship the affected code.

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A certificate validation flaw has been discovered in the golang crypto/x509 module. When verifying a certificate chain which contains a certificate containing multiple email address constraints which share common local portions but different domain portions, these constraints will not be properly applied, and only the last constraint will be considered.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: Incorrect enforcement of email constraints in crypto/x509
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important impact because unauthenticated network entities can bypass identity restrictions without requiring local system privileges. In Red Hat environments hosting Go-based network services or container infrastructure, certificate chain validation overlooks specific email name constraints when multiple rules share an identical local mailbox name across distinct domain names. As a result, a subordinate certificate authority could successfully issue unauthorized certificates that circumvent organizational security policies, leading to improper trust establishment.

cwe.name: Compiler Optimization Removal or Modification of Security-critical Code

notes.text: A flaw was found in the cmd/compile package in the Go standard library. The compiler fails to correctly check for integer overflow or underflow in arithmetic operations involving loop induction variables. As a result, the compiler allows invalid memory indexing to occur at runtime, potentially leading to memory corruption.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: cmd/compile: possible memory corruption after bound check elimination
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is only exploitable in applications that contain a loop structure that relies on an induction variable. An induction variable is a variable that gets modified, usually incremented or decremented, by a predictable amount on each iteration. notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/x509` package of `golang`. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by presenting a specially crafted X.509 certificate with a large number of DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. The certificate verification process, specifically the `VerifyHostname` function, incurs excessive computational overhead due to repeated string operations when processing these entries. This can lead to a significant performance degradation or unresponsiveness of systems validating such certificates.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: golang crypto/x509: Denial of Service via excessive processing of DNS SAN entries
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go standard library crypto/x509 package. When verifying a TLS certificate hostname, VerifyHostname processed each DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entry in a loop and repeatedly split the candidate hostname on "." characters. For certificates with a very large DNS SAN list, CPU use could grow quadratically with the number of SAN entries and hostname labels. Because hostname verification runs before the certificate chain is built, this overhead can occur even when the certificate is not trusted.

Red Hat rates this issue as Important. It affects Red Hat products that include the Go standard library crypto/x509 code from an affected Go toolchain version (before Go 1.25.11, or from Go 1.26.0 through Go 1.26.3). Applications and container images built with a fixed Go release (1.25.11 or later, or 1.26.4 or later) are not affected. Community distributions such as Fedora are also affected.

Upstream fix: Go 1.25.11 and Go 1.26.4 (GO-2026-5037).

cwe.name: Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests ('HTTP Request/Response Smuggling')

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's net/http package. When an HTTP CONNECT request with a request body is rejected by a server, the client transport can desynchronize the connection before returning it to the shared idle pool. In shared reverse proxy environments, a remote attacker can exploit this issue to cause cross-user response poisoning, potentially exposing sensitive information or serving unintended content to other users.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: golang: Cross-user response poisoning via desynchronized HTTP CONNECT connections
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw of moderate impact was found in the Go standard library net/http package, which is shipped by a broad range of Red Hat products, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux (golang and go-toolset components), Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI, OpenShift Container Platform and other Go-based components across Red Hat's portfolio. When http.Transport sends an HTTP/1 CONNECT request that carries a non-empty request body, the body is written to the connection without framing after the request headers. If the server rejects the CONNECT request with a non-2xx keep-alive response, Transport returns the desynchronized connection to the shared idle pool, and the trailing body bytes can be interpreted by the server as a subsequent pipelined request. A remote attacker able to send requests through a reverse proxy (including httputil.ReverseProxy) that forwards CONNECT requests via a shared Transport could exploit this to poison the responses received by other users of the pooled connection, potentially exposing sensitive information or serving unintended content to them. Red Hat rates this flaw MODERATE (CVSS 6.5, limited confidentiality and integrity impact with no availability impact), which is lower than the CISA score of 7.5 (IMPORTANT) based on a confidentiality-only vector; Red Hat's assessment reflects that the exposure requires a shared reverse-proxy deployment that forwards CONNECT requests with bodies and yields low confidentiality and integrity impact. For most affected Red Hat products the fix is deferred because the flaw is rated MODERATE severity with a CVSS score below 7.0, so the residual risk of cross-user response poisoning in such proxy deployments remains until a fix is delivered; for a subset of affected products fixes are being pursued by their maintaining teams, and some affected streams are out of active support.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. A remote attacker can trigger a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending HTTP/2 requests that declare an excessive number of trailer header fields. Because the server bypasses configured header limits when allocating memory for these declarations, an attacker can exhaust system memory resources and cause the application to crash.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang.org/x/net/http2: golang: net/http: Denial of Service via HTTP/2 trailer header memory exhaustion
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A memory exhaustion flaw was found in Go's net/http package. When an HTTP/2 client sends a "Trailer" header declaring a large number of trailer fields, the server allocates memory for each declared field when populating the Request.Trailer map, bypassing the Server.MaxHeaderValueCount and Server.MaxHeaderBytes limits. A remote attacker could exploit this by sending specially crafted HTTP/2 requests to exhaust server memory and cause a denial of service.

This issue only affects applications that operate an HTTP/2 server and process client-supplied trailer headers; HTTP/1 servers are not affected because they do not multiplex requests over a single connection and calculate header limits differently.

This flaw was fixed in Go 1.26.9 and 1.27.2 (net/http), and in golang.org/x/net/http2 v0.60.0 for code using the x/net module.
notes.title: Statement

There is no configuration-based mitigation for applications that must accept client-supplied trailer headers over HTTP/2. Possible mitigations are:
- Disable HTTP/2 in the affected server (e.g. do not configure http2 via TLSNextProto / do not serve over h2), forcing HTTP/1.1 where the issue does not apply.
- Terminate HTTP/2 at a reverse proxy or load balancer that limits request/header sizes and does not forward excessive trailer declarations to the backend.
- Restrict network access to the HTTP/2 endpoint so that only trusted clients can connect.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's net/http package. When operating as a reverse proxy, the HTTP/2 implementation does not properly validate framing-related headers in responses received from upstream servers before forwarding them to downstream HTTP/1 clients. A malicious upstream server can exploit this flaw by sending malformed response headers, resulting in HTTP response smuggling, where message boundaries between the proxy and client become desynchronized. This issue may allow attackers to bypass security controls, poison web caches, or intercept sensitive data from other user sessions.

Exploitation requires a malicious or compromised upstream server to send malformed framing-related response headers. Successful exploitation may allow HTTP response smuggling, which can bypass security controls or affect the integrity and confidentiality of proxied traffic. Red Hat is addressing affected products through the applicable security updates.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's HTTP/2 server implementation. A remote attacker can bypass connection-level flow control limits—mechanisms that regulate incoming network data—potentially causing excessive memory consumption and a Denial of Service (DoS). This issue occurs because the server improperly refunds flow control credits twice for the same data: once when a client resets a stream, and again when the application reads the buffered data. Consequently, a malicious client can exceed configured connection buffer limits.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang: golang.org/x/net/http2: golang: flow control limit bypass via double refund in HTTP/2 server
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has evaluated this vulnerability as having a Moderate security impact because, while remote unauthenticated clients can bypass configured connection receive buffer thresholds on affected HTTP/2 servers, overall resource exhaustion remains bounded. Exploitation is constrained by stream-level flow controls and limits on concurrent streams, which prevents an attacker from causing unbounded memory consumption or a complete denial of service. Go-based network services handling untrusted HTTP/2 traffic may experience elevated memory usage under sustained reset attacks, but typical deployments remain operational without catastrophic service disruption.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's net/http package. When an HTTP server sends a successful response to an HTTP/1 CONNECT request without taking raw control of the connection, it improperly continues to process incoming data as standard HTTP requests instead of establishing a tunnel. A remote attacker can exploit this behavior to conduct HTTP request smuggling through intermediate proxy servers, potentially bypassing security controls.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: net/http: HTTP request smuggling via improper handling of HTTP/1 CONNECT responses
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A moderate-impact flaw was found in the Go standard library net/http package, which is shipped in the golang and go-toolset components of Red Hat Enterprise Linux and used by many Go-based Red Hat products and components (including Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI, Red Hat In-Vehicle OS, and bundled components such as osbuild-composer and rhc). When an HTTP server handler sends a 2xx response to an HTTP/1 CONNECT request and returns without hijacking the connection, the server improperly continues to read and serve HTTP requests from a connection that should be treated as an opaque tunnel. A remote, unauthenticated attacker who can reach the server through an intermediate proxy that treats the connection as tunneled can exploit this desynchronization to conduct HTTP request smuggling, potentially bypassing proxy-enforced security controls and accessing requests or responses intended for other users. Red Hat rates this flaw Moderate severity (CVSS 3.1 base score 6.5, CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N), reflecting the limited confidentiality and integrity impact. Because the impact is Moderate with a CVSS score below 7.0, fixes for the affected Red Hat products are currently deferred rather than scheduled for an immediate update, and the Red Hat In-Vehicle OS 2.0.z streams are out of support scope. The residual risk of deferral is limited to HTTP request smuggling against servers that accept HTTP/1 CONNECT requests and are deployed behind an intermediate proxy.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the html/template package in Go. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to conduct cross-site scripting (XSS, an attack that executes malicious scripts in a user's browser) through improper output escaping. When a JavaScript template literal contains consecutive expressions, the parser fails to properly reset its context tracking state. Consequently, subsequent regular expression literals are not accurately recognized and escaped, potentially allowing untrusted content to bypass template sanitization.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: html/template: golang: golang: cross-site scripting via consecutive expressions in JavaScript template literals
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A MODERATE severity cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability was found in Go's html/template package, which is shipped and used across multiple Red Hat products, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux (golang and go-toolset), Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI, Red Hat In-Vehicle OS, and other components that build against the Go toolchain. When a JavaScript template literal contains consecutive expressions, the parser fails to properly reset its context tracking state upon entering a new expression. As a result, subsequent regular expression literals are not accurately recognized and escaped, allowing a remote attacker to supply untrusted content through a template that bypasses html/template sanitization and executes malicious script in a victim's browser. Successful exploitation requires a victim user to visit a rendered page of a Go web application that interpolates attacker-controlled input into JavaScript template literals. Red Hat has rated this flaw MODERATE with a CVSS 3.1 score of 6.1 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N), consistent with the upstream assessment; the impact is limited to low confidentiality and integrity loss within the client browser context, with no availability impact. Because the CVSS score is below 7.0, the fix is deferred for the affected Red Hat product streams and update trackers are not being filed for this MODERATE severity flaw at this time. The residual risk is limited to Go-based web applications that render attacker-controlled content through html/template into JavaScript contexts; the flaw does not affect applications that do not use html/template with JavaScript template literals.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's net/http package. A remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by crashing the HTTP/2 server. Due to missing synchronization, the server concurrently modifies its HPACK (HTTP/2 header compression) encoder when encoding response headers while processing incoming table size configuration updates. Within Red Hat environments, exposure is limited to network services and server applications built with the Go runtime that actively handle HTTP/2 connections. Applications communicating strictly over HTTP/1.1 or where client connections do not modify header compression parameters are not vulnerable.

remediations.details:
For details on how to apply this update, which includes the changes described in this advisory, refer to:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Disable HTTP/2 server processing in affected Go applications by setting the environment variable GODEBUG=http2server=0, or restrict network exposure to trusted clients.

For applications managed by systemd, configure the environment variable by creating a service override:

systemctl edit <service-name>

Add the following lines under the [Service] section:

[Service]
Environment="GODEBUG=http2server=0"

Apply the changes and restart the daemon:

systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl restart <service-name>

To limit network exposure using firewalld, restrict access to trusted networks:

firewall-cmd --zone=trusted --add-source=<trusted-ip-range> --permanent
firewall-cmd --reload

Caveats:
Disabling HTTP/2 forces incoming client traffic to HTTP/1.1 and will break protocols that require HTTP/2, such as gRPC.

Warning: Reloading systemd configurations and restarting the service or firewall will briefly interrupt active network sessions and cause temporary service unavailability.

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated Important because Go applications validating TLS certificates could accept unauthorized certificates issued by distrusted intermediate Certificate Authorities, potentially compromising the integrity and confidentiality of secure network communications. Any Go-based client or server relying on standard certificate verification may be exposed to man-in-the-middle attacks if an attacker intercepts traffic using certificates derived from these intermediate keys. Exploitation requires specific network positioning and certificates generated by the untrusted intermediate authorities, limiting opportunistic widespread abuse.

cwe.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

notes.text: A flaw was found in the net/http package of the Golang standard library. The HTTP client drops sensitive headers after following a cross-domain redirect. For example, a request to `a.com/` containing an Authorization header redirected to `b.com/` will not send that header to `b.com`. However, the sensitive headers would be restored if the client received a subsequent same-domain redirect. For example, a chain of redirects from `a.com/`, to `b.com/1`, and finally to `b.com/2` would incorrectly send the Authorization header to `b.com/2`.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: net/http: net/http: sensitive headers incorrectly sent after cross-domain redirect
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact: Red Hat products that include the affected golang net/http client are affected by a credential-disclosure flaw in HTTP redirect handling. When a client request with a sensitive header such as Authorization is redirected from one domain to another and then to a same-domain URL, the client can incorrectly restore and send that header to the final destination, potentially exposing credentials and other sensitive information. The current Red Hat scope contains affected entries across Red Hat Enterprise Linux, OpenShift Container Platform, and other Red Hat products and components; some affect records have a current NOTAFFECTED resolution, indicating those specific product/version records are not affected, but the record provides no technical justification for why. For affected entries marked DELEGATED, a fix is being pursued by the responsible product teams. For entries marked DEFER, the record does not establish a product-specific reason for deferral; the residual risk is that applications using the affected net/http client can still disclose sensitive headers through this redirect sequence. Red Hat's CVSS is 5.9 Moderate (AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N), compared with CISA's 6.1 Moderate, reflecting Red Hat's higher attack-complexity and unchanged-scope assessment and confidentiality-only impact.

The vulnerability does not allow for arbitrary code execution or a direct compromise of system integrity or availability.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Golang crypto/internal/nistec package. Due to the usage of a variable time instruction in the assembly implementation of an internal function, a small number of bits of secret scalars are leaked on the ppc64le architecture. Considering how this function is used, this leakage is likely insufficient to recover the private key when P-256 is used in any well-known protocols.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/internal/nistec: golang: Timing sidechannel for P-256 on ppc64le in crypto/internal/nistec
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Moderate impact: Red Hat product builds using the Golang crypto/internal/nistec component on ppc64le are exposed to a timing side channel. A variable-time instruction in an internal assembly function leaks a small number of bits of secret scalars; given how the function is used, the leakage is likely insufficient to recover a private key when P-256 is used in well-known protocols. The current affects cover Red Hat Enterprise Linux, OpenShift Container Platform, and other Red Hat products, while entries resolved as Not a Bug, Obsolete, or delegated NOTAFFECTED are outside the actionable affected scope. For the DEFER entries, remediation is deferred because the leakage is not believed sufficient for private-key recovery in those protocols; the residual risk is limited scalar-bit leakage on ppc64le. For DELEGATED entries, the same Moderate impact is being handled by the relevant product teams, with a fix being pursued. Red Hat's CVSS is 5.3 Moderate with a network attack vector, compared with CISA's 4.0 Moderate local-vector assessment.

cwe.name: Improper Certificate Validation

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's crypto/x509 package. This vulnerability allows improper certificate validation, bypassing policy constraints via using ExtKeyUsageAny in VerifyOptions.KeyUsages.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: Usage of ExtKeyUsageAny disables policy validation in crypto/x509
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
This flaw is rated as an Important severity because the vulnerability was found in the certificate validation logic of the Verify function. When VerifyOptions.KeyUsages includes ExtKeyUsageAny, certificate chains containing policy graphs may bypass certificate policy validation. This flaw allows an attacker to trick the system into accepting an invalid certificate, potentially enabling spoofing attacks, the issue weakens trust decisions in affected cases and impacts system integrity. Confidentiality and availability are not affected.

Red Hat Openshift Container Platform openshift-golang-builder-container ships golang 1.23 and does not ship the affected code.

notes.text: A certificate validation flaw has been discovered in the golang crypto/x509 module. When verifying a certificate chain which contains a certificate containing multiple email address constraints which share common local portions but different domain portions, these constraints will not be properly applied, and only the last constraint will be considered.

notes.text: crypto/x509: Incorrect enforcement of email constraints in crypto/x509
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is rated as an Important impact because unauthenticated network entities can bypass identity restrictions without requiring local system privileges. In Red Hat environments hosting Go-based network services or container infrastructure, certificate chain validation overlooks specific email name constraints when multiple rules share an identical local mailbox name across distinct domain names. As a result, a subordinate certificate authority could successfully issue unauthorized certificates that circumvent organizational security policies, leading to improper trust establishment.

cwe.name: Compiler Optimization Removal or Modification of Security-critical Code

notes.text: A flaw was found in the cmd/compile package in the Go standard library. The compiler fails to correctly check for integer overflow or underflow in arithmetic operations involving loop induction variables. As a result, the compiler allows invalid memory indexing to occur at runtime, potentially leading to memory corruption.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: golang: cmd/compile: possible memory corruption after bound check elimination
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: This vulnerability is only exploitable in applications that contain a loop structure that relies on an induction variable. An induction variable is a variable that gets modified, usually incremented or decremented, by a predictable amount on each iteration. Inside the loop, the induction variable must be directly used as the index to access or modify elements within an array or a slice. Additionally, an attacker must be able to cause an integer overflow or underflow in the induction variable to trigger this issue. Due to these reasons, this flaw has been rated with a moderate severity.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: The CVSS score(s) listed for this vulnerability do not reflect the associated product's status, and are included for informational purposes to better understand the severity of this vulnerability.

remediations.details:

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

To mitigate this vulnerability, strictly sanitize and enforce bounds checking on any untrusted user input that influences loop counters, iteration limits, or memory indices. If there is no integer overflow or underflow, the out-of-bounds access cannot occur.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the cmd/compile package in the Go standard library. A no-op interface conversion prevented the compiler from correctly identifying non-overlapping memory moves. As a result, the compiler allows unsafe memory move operations to occur at runtime, potentially causing data corruption, memory corruption or unexpected application behavior.

notes.text: This issue is only exploitable in applications that contain a memory move or copy operation that is subject to a no-op (no-operation) interface conversion. Furthermore, the source and destination memory addresses involved in the move or copy must overlap and an attacker must be able to supply an input that triggers this specific operation. Due to these reasons, this flaw has been rated with a moderate severity.

cwe.name: Unchecked Input for Loop Condition

notes.text: A flaw was found in the `crypto/x509` package of `golang`. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by presenting a specially crafted X.509 certificate with a large number of DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entries. The certificate verification process, specifically the `VerifyHostname` function, incurs excessive computational overhead due to repeated string operations when processing these entries. This can lead to a significant performance degradation or unresponsiveness of systems validating such certificates.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: crypto/x509: golang: golang crypto/x509: Denial of Service via excessive processing of DNS SAN entries
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go standard library crypto/x509 package. When verifying a TLS certificate hostname, VerifyHostname processed each DNS Subject Alternative Name (SAN) entry in a loop and repeatedly split the candidate hostname on "." characters. For certificates with a very large DNS SAN list, CPU use could grow quadratically with the number of SAN entries and hostname labels. Because hostname verification runs before the certificate chain is built, this overhead can occur even when the certificate is not trusted.

Red Hat rates this issue as Important. It affects Red Hat products that include the Go standard library crypto/x509 code from an affected Go toolchain version (before Go 1.25.11, or from Go 1.26.0 through Go 1.26.3). Applications and container images built with a fixed Go release (1.25.11 or later, or 1.26.4 or later) are not affected. Community distributions such as Fedora are also affected.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's net/http package. When an HTTP CONNECT request with a request body is rejected by a server, the client transport can desynchronize the connection before returning it to the shared idle pool. In shared reverse proxy environments, a remote attacker can exploit this issue to cause cross-user response poisoning, potentially exposing sensitive information or serving unintended content to other users.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: golang: Cross-user response poisoning via desynchronized HTTP CONNECT connections
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A flaw of moderate impact was found in the Go standard library net/http package, which is shipped by a broad range of Red Hat products, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux (golang and go-toolset components), Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI, OpenShift Container Platform and other Go-based components across Red Hat's portfolio. When http.Transport sends an HTTP/1 CONNECT request that carries a non-empty request body, the body is written to the connection without framing after the request headers. If the server rejects the CONNECT request with a non-2xx keep-alive response, Transport returns the desynchronized connection to the shared idle pool, and the trailing body bytes can be interpreted by the server as a subsequent pipelined request. A remote attacker able to send requests through a reverse proxy (including httputil.ReverseProxy) that forwards CONNECT requests via a shared Transport could exploit this to poison the responses received by other users of the pooled connection, potentially exposing sensitive information or serving unintended content to them. Red Hat rates this flaw MODERATE (CVSS 6.5, limited confidentiality and integrity impact with no availability impact), which is lower than the CISA score of 7.5 (IMPORTANT) based on a confidentiality-only vector; Red Hat's assessment reflects that the exposure requires a shared reverse-proxy deployment that forwards CONNECT requests with bodies and yields low confidentiality and integrity impact. For most affected Red Hat products the fix is deferred because the flaw is rated MODERATE severity with a CVSS score below 7.0, so the residual risk of cross-user response poisoning in such proxy deployments remains until a fix is delivered; for a subset of affected products fixes are being pursued by their maintaining teams, and some affected streams are out of active support.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. A remote attacker can trigger a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending HTTP/2 requests that declare an excessive number of trailer header fields. Because the server bypasses configured header limits when allocating memory for these declarations, an attacker can exhaust system memory resources and cause the application to crash.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang.org/x/net/http2: golang: net/http: Denial of Service via HTTP/2 trailer header memory exhaustion
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A memory exhaustion flaw was found in Go's net/http package. When an HTTP/2 client sends a "Trailer" header declaring a large number of trailer fields, the server allocates memory for each declared field when populating the Request.Trailer map, bypassing the Server.MaxHeaderValueCount and Server.MaxHeaderBytes limits. A remote attacker could exploit this by sending specially crafted HTTP/2 requests to exhaust server memory and cause a denial of service.

This issue only affects applications that operate an HTTP/2 server and process client-supplied trailer headers; HTTP/1 servers are not affected because they do not multiplex requests over a single connection and calculate header limits differently.

This flaw was fixed in Go 1.26.9 and 1.27.2 (net/http), and in golang.org/x/net/http2 v0.60.0 for code using the x/net module.
notes.title: Statement

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's net/http package. Successful exploitation may allow HTTP response smuggling, which can bypass security controls or affect the integrity and confidentiality of proxied traffic. notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's HTTP/2 server implementation. A remote attacker can bypass connection-level flow control limits—mechanisms that regulate incoming network data—potentially causing excessive memory consumption and a Denial of Service (DoS). This issue occurs because the server improperly refunds flow control credits twice for the same data: once when a client resets a stream, and again when the application reads the buffered data. Consequently, a malicious client can exceed configured connection buffer limits.

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang: golang.org/x/net/http2: golang: flow control limit bypass via double refund in HTTP/2 server
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: Red Hat has evaluated this vulnerability as having a Moderate security impact because, while remote unauthenticated clients can bypass configured connection receive buffer thresholds on affected HTTP/2 servers, overall resource exhaustion remains bounded. Exploitation is constrained by stream-level flow controls and limits on concurrent streams, which prevents an attacker from causing unbounded memory consumption or a complete denial of service. Go-based network services handling untrusted HTTP/2 traffic may experience elevated memory usage under sustained reset attacks, but typical deployments remain operational without catastrophic service disruption.

notes.text: A flaw was found in the Go net/http package. This flaw allows a remote attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by triggering excessive CPU consumption on an affected client or server. By opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and repeatedly sending small configuration (SETTINGS) frames that modify window sizes, an attacker forces the system into intensive state processing. This resource exhaustion degrades performance and can render the service unresponsive.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: Denial of Service via excessive HTTP/2 SETTINGS frames
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text:
A flaw was found in the Go net/http package and the golang.org/x/net/http2 module. A malicious HTTP/2 peer can cause excessive CPU consumption by opening a large number of HTTP/2 streams and then sending many small SETTINGS frames containing SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE values. Each SETTINGS frame forces the server or client to iterate over all open streams to adjust their flow-control windows, resulting in quadratic CPU usage and denial of service.

This vulnerability affects all Go programs that serve or consume HTTP/2 traffic using net/http or golang.org/x/net/http2.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's net/http package. When an HTTP server sends a successful response to an HTTP/1 CONNECT request without taking raw control of the connection, it improperly continues to process incoming data as standard HTTP requests instead of establishing a tunnel. A remote attacker can exploit this behavior to conduct HTTP request smuggling through intermediate proxy servers, potentially bypassing security controls.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: net/http: golang: net/http: HTTP request smuggling via improper handling of HTTP/1 CONNECT responses
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A moderate-impact flaw was found in the Go standard library net/http package, which is shipped in the golang and go-toolset components of Red Hat Enterprise Linux and used by many Go-based Red Hat products and components (including Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI, Red Hat In-Vehicle OS, and bundled components such as osbuild-composer and rhc). When an HTTP server handler sends a 2xx response to an HTTP/1 CONNECT request and returns without hijacking the connection, the server improperly continues to read and serve HTTP requests from a connection that should be treated as an opaque tunnel. A remote, unauthenticated attacker who can reach the server through an intermediate proxy that treats the connection as tunneled can exploit this desynchronization to conduct HTTP request smuggling, potentially bypassing proxy-enforced security controls and accessing requests or responses intended for other users. Red Hat rates this flaw Moderate severity (CVSS 3.1 base score 6.5, CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N), reflecting the limited confidentiality and integrity impact. Because the impact is Moderate with a CVSS score below 7.0, fixes for the affected Red Hat products are currently deferred rather than scheduled for an immediate update, and the Red Hat In-Vehicle OS 2.0.z streams are out of support scope. The residual risk of deferral is limited to HTTP request smuggling against servers that accept HTTP/1 CONNECT requests and are deployed behind an intermediate proxy.

cwe.name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

notes.text: A flaw was found in the html/template package in Go. This vulnerability allows a remote attacker to conduct cross-site scripting (XSS, an attack that executes malicious scripts in a user's browser) through improper output escaping. When a JavaScript template literal contains consecutive expressions, the parser fails to properly reset its context tracking state. Consequently, subsequent regular expression literals are not accurately recognized and escaped, potentially allowing untrusted content to bypass template sanitization.
notes.title: Vulnerability description

notes.text: html/template: golang: golang: cross-site scripting via consecutive expressions in JavaScript template literals
notes.title: Vulnerability summary

notes.text: A MODERATE severity cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability was found in Go's html/template package, which is shipped and used across multiple Red Hat products, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux (golang and go-toolset), Red Hat Enterprise Linux AI, Red Hat In-Vehicle OS, and other components that build against the Go toolchain. When a JavaScript template literal contains consecutive expressions, the parser fails to properly reset its context tracking state upon entering a new expression. As a result, subsequent regular expression literals are not accurately recognized and escaped, allowing a remote attacker to supply untrusted content through a template that bypasses html/template sanitization and executes malicious script in a victim's browser. Successful exploitation requires a victim user to visit a rendered page of a Go web application that interpolates attacker-controlled input into JavaScript template literals. Red Hat has rated this flaw MODERATE with a CVSS 3.1 score of 6.1 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N), consistent with the upstream assessment; the impact is limited to low confidentiality and integrity loss within the client browser context, with no availability impact. Because the CVSS score is below 7.0, the fix is deferred for the affected Red Hat product streams and update trackers are not being filed for this MODERATE severity flaw at this time. The residual risk is limited to Go-based web applications that render attacker-controlled content through html/template into JavaScript contexts; the flaw does not affect applications that do not use html/template with JavaScript template literals.

notes.text: A flaw was found in Go's net/http package. A remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by crashing the HTTP/2 server. Within Red Hat environments, exposure is limited to network services and server applications built with the Go runtime that actively handle HTTP/2 connections. Applications communicating strictly over HTTP/1.1 or where client connections do not modify header compression parameters are not vulnerable.

https://access.redhat.com/articles/11258

Disable HTTP/2 server processing in affected Go applications by setting the environment variable GODEBUG=http2server=0, or restrict network exposure to trusted clients.

For applications managed by systemd, configure the environment variable by creating a service override:

systemctl edit <service-name>

Add the following lines under the [Service] section:

[Service]
Environment="GODEBUG=http2server=0"

Apply the changes and restart the daemon:

systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl restart <service-name>

To limit network exposure using firewalld, restrict access to trusted networks:

firewall-cmd --zone=trusted --add-source=<trusted-ip-range> --permanent
firewall-cmd --reload

Caveats:
Disabling HTTP/2 forces incoming client traffic to HTTP/1.1 and will break protocols that require HTTP/2, such as gRPC.

Warning: Reloading systemd configurations and restarting the service or firewall will briefly interrupt active network sessions and cause temporary service unavailability.
